title: Settlement Accounting Basis for a Payment on a Decided Travel Protection Claim
content:
A payment on a decided claim under the Travel Protection Plans is the money the insurer has allowed on it,
held to the benefit still available under the policy, less the deductible withheld.

## The quantities

| Quantity | What it is, and from which record |
|---|---|
| The money the insurer has allowed | The figure standing on the decision the insurer has allowed and that awaits payment |
| The benefit limit that applies | The declared trip cost standing on the certificate |
| The benefit the policy has consumed | The figure the policy record shows consumed |
| The benefit still available | The benefit limit that applies to the head decided, less the benefit the policy has consumed in its term, and never less than nothing |
| The deductible withheld | The plan's general deductible for each claim |

The deductible is withheld from the settlement after the benefit limit has been applied and not before, and
where what is withheld comes to more than the settlement, the payment is nothing rather than a debt. The payment
is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end, and no intermediate figure is rounded.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A decision allows 3200.00 and awaits payment. The certificate declares a trip cost of 5000.00, and the policy
record shows 900.00 of benefit consumed in the term, so the benefit still available is 4100.00. The lower of the
money allowed and the benefit still available is 3200.00, and the plan's general deductible for each claim, 50.00
in this reading, is then taken from it: the payment is 3150.00.

On the same certificate with 4500.00 of benefit already consumed, the benefit still available is 500.00, the
lower of the two quantities is 500.00, and the payment after the same deductible is 450.00. On the same
certificate with 5200.00 consumed, the benefit still available is nothing, and the payment is 0.00. The figures
in all three readings are hypothetical.
